                    ### Question
                    A 54-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by a nurse 30 minutes after receiving scheduled radiation therapy for papillary thyroid cancer. After the radioisotope was ingested, the physician realized that a much larger fixed dose was given instead of the appropriate dose based on radiation dosimetry. Which of the following pharmacotherapies should be administered immediately to prevent complications from this exposure?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Propylthiouracil
opb. Mercaptoethanesulfonate
opc. Potassium iodide
opd. Methimazole
ope. Dexrazoxane

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the case of excessive radiation exposure leading to potential thyroid gland damage and subsequent release of high levels of thyroid hormones, immediate administration of potassium iodide is recommended to block thyroid hormone synthesis and prevent complications such as thyroid storm. This is supported by the consensus understanding that potassium iodide can help mitigate the effects of excessive radiation exposure on the thyroid gland.
